6356:+/-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/
6357:+
6358:+/-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
6359:+`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
6360:+theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6361:+    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AA'.side)) :
6362:+    S.place .AA' O =
6363:+      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
6364:+        (heteroKron O
6365:+          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
6366:+            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
6367:+  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm
6368:+
6369:+/-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
6370:+`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
6371:+theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6372:+    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
6373:+    S.place .BA'' O =
6374:+      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
6375:+        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
6376:+          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
6377:+  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_right S O).symm
6378:+
6379:+/-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
6380:+`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
6381:+theorem place_AB''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6382:+    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AB''.side)) :
6383:+    S.place .AB'' O =
6384:+      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
6385:+        (heteroKron O
6386:+          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
6387:+            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
6388:+  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm
6389:+
6390:+/-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
6391:+`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
6392:+theorem place_BB'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6393:+    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BB'.side)) :
6394:+    S.place .BB' O =
6395:+      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
6396:+        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
6397:+          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
6398:+  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_right S O).symm
6399:+
6400:+/-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
6401:+theorem reindexOp_conjTranspose {ι κ : Type*} (e : ι ≃ κ) (M : Op κ) :
6402:+    reindexOp e Mᴴ = (reindexOp e M)ᴴ := by
6403:+  ext i j
6404:+  rfl
6405:+
6406:+/-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
6407:+theorem reindexOp_nonneg {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
6408:+    (e : ι ≃ κ) {M : Op κ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
6409:+    0 ≤ reindexOp e M := by
6410:+  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
6411:+  letI := Fintype.ofFinite κ
6412:+  rw [Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef] at hM ⊢
6413:+  exact hM.submatrix e.symm.symm
6414:+
6415:+/-! ## The placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism -/
6416:+
6417:+set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
6418:+/-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
6419:+theorem place_mul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
6420:+    ∀ (p : Placement) (A B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
6421:+      S.place p (A * B) = S.place p A * S.place p B
6422:+  | .AA', A, B => by
6423:+      classical
6424:+      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq,
6425:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
6426:+      all_goals rfl
6427:+  | .BA'', A, B => by
6428:+      classical
6429:+      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq,
6430:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
6431:+        mul_one, mul_one]
6432:+      all_goals rfl
6433:+  | .BB', A, B => by
6434:+      classical
6435:+      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq,
6436:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
6437:+        mul_one, mul_one]
6438:+      all_goals rfl
6439:+  | .AB'', A, B => by
6440:+      classical
6441:+      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq,
6442:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
6443:+      all_goals rfl
6444:+
6445:+/-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
6446:+space. -/
6447:+theorem place_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :
6448:+    S.place p (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) = 1 := by
6449:+  ext i j
6450:+  cases p <;>
6451:+    · simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.one_apply, Prod.ext_iff]
6452:+      split_ifs <;> simp_all
6453:+
6454:+/-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators. -/
6455:+theorem place_finsetSum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {γ : Type*}
6456:+    (s : Finset γ) (O : γ → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
6457:+    S.place p (∑ x ∈ s, O x) = ∑ x ∈ s, S.place p (O x) := by
6458:+  ext i j
6459:+  cases p <;>
6460:+    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul,
6461:+      Finset.mul_sum]
6462:+
6463:+/-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
6464:+theorem place_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
6465:+    ∀ (p : Placement) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
6466:+      S.place p Aᴴ = (S.place p A)ᴴ
6467:+  | .AA', A => by
6468:+      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
6469:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
6470:+      all_goals rfl
6471:+  | .BA'', A => by
6472:+      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
6473:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
6474:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
6475:+        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
6476:+      all_goals rfl
6477:+  | .BB', A => by
6478:+      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
6479:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
6480:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
6481:+        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
6482:+      all_goals rfl
6483:+  | .AB'', A => by
6484:+      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
6485:+        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
6486:+      all_goals rfl

6488:+set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
6489:+/-- A placement preserves positivity. -/
6490:+theorem place_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
6491:+    ∀ (p : Placement) {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)}, 0 ≤ A →
6492:+      0 ≤ S.place p A
6493:+  | .AA', A, hA => by
6494:+      classical
6495:+      rw [place_AA'_eq]
6496:+      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA
6497:+        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg))
6498:+  | .BA'', A, hA => by
6499:+      classical
6500:+      rw [place_BA''_eq]
6501:+      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
6502:+        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
6503:+        (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)))
6504:+  | .BB', A, hA => by
6505:+      classical
6506:+      rw [place_BB'_eq]
6507:+      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
6508:+        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
6509:+        (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)))
6510:+  | .AB'', A, hA => by
6511:+      classical
6512:+      rw [place_AB''_eq]
6513:+      exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA
6514:+        (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg))

6516:+/-- The placement of a local operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
6517:+the identity. -/
6518:+theorem place_le_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
6519:+    {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hA : A ≤ 1) :
6520:+    S.place p A ≤ 1 := by
6521:+  have h : 0 ≤ S.place p (1 - A) := S.place_nonneg p (sub_nonneg.mpr hA)
6522:+  rw [place_sub, place_one] at h
6523:+  exact sub_nonneg.mp h
6524:+
6525:+/-- The placement of a projector is a contraction. -/
6526:+theorem place_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6527:+    (p : Placement) {E : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hE : IsProj E) :
6528:+    (S.place p E)ᴴ * S.place p E ≤ 1 := by
6529:+  rw [← place_conjTranspose, ← place_mul, hE.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
6530:+    hE.isIdempotentElem.eq]
6531:+  exact S.place_le_one p (sub_nonneg.mp hE.one_sub.nonneg)

6533:+set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
6534:+/-- Operators placed on opposite register pairs commute. -/
6535:+theorem place_comm (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
6536:+    ∀ (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
6537:+      ∀ (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
6538:+        (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)),
6539:+        S.place p₁ A * S.place p₂ B = S.place p₂ B * S.place p₁ A
6540:+  | .AA', .BA'', _, A, B => by
6541:+      classical
6542:+      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
6543:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
6544:+      simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
6545:+  | .BA'', .AA', _, A, B => by
6546:+      classical
6547:+      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
6548:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
6549:+      simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
6550:+  | .BB', .AB'', _, A, B => by
6551:+      classical
6552:+      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
6553:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
6554:+      simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
6555:+  | .AB'', .BB', _, A, B => by
6556:+      classical
6557:+      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
6558:+        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
6559:+      simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
6560:+  | .AA', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6561:+  | .AA', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6562:+  | .AA', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6563:+  | .BA'', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6564:+  | .BA'', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6565:+  | .BA'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6566:+  | .BB', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6567:+  | .BB', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6568:+  | .BB', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6569:+  | .AB'', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6570:+  | .AB'', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
6571:+  | .AB'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h

6573:+/-- A complete measurement on a local expanded space, placed on one of the
6574:+four register pairs, is a complete measurement on the six-register space. -/
6575:+def placedMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {α : Type*}
6576:+    [Fintype α] (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
6577:+    Measurement α (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
6578:+  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (fun a => S.place p (M.effect a))
6579:+    (fun a => S.place_nonneg p (M.pos a))
6580:+    (by rw [← place_finsetSum, M.sum_eq_one, place_one])
6581:+
6582:+/-- The effects of a placed measurement are the placed effects. -/
6583:+@[simp] theorem placedMeasurement_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6584:+    (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
6585:+    (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) (a : α) :
6586:+    (S.placedMeasurement p M).effect a = S.place p (M.effect a) := rfl
6587:+
6588:+/-- A placed projective measurement is projective. -/
6589:+theorem placedMeasurement_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6590:+    (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
6591:+    (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
6592:+    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
6593:+    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.placedMeasurement p M) := by
6594:+  intro a
6595:+  refine isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩
6596:+  · change S.place p (M.effect a) * S.place p (M.effect a) =
6597:+      S.place p (M.effect a)
6598:+    rw [← place_mul, (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
6599:+  · change star (S.place p (M.effect a)) = S.place p (M.effect a)
6600:+    rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, ← place_conjTranspose,
6601:+      (hM a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
6602:+
6603:+/-- A placement maps the zero operator to zero. -/
6604:+theorem place_zero (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :
6605:+    S.place p (0 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) = 0 := by
6606:+  ext i j
6607:+  cases p <;> simp [ProjectiveSetting.place]

6609:+/-- The completed expanded point measurement agrees with the original effect
6610:+at a defined outcome. -/
6611:+theorem pointMeasExpOption_effect_some (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6612:+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
6613:+    (a : PauliScalar P) :
6614:+    (S.pointMeasExpOption side W u).effect (some a) =
6615:+      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a := by
6616:+  classical
6617:+  unfold ProjectiveSetting.pointMeasExpOption
6618:+  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
6619:+  simp [Finset.filter_eq']
6620:+
6621:+/-- The completed expanded point measurement has zero effect at `none`. -/
6622:+theorem pointMeasExpOption_effect_none (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
6623:+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
6624:+    (S.pointMeasExpOption side W u).effect none = 0 := by
6625:+  classical
6626:+  unfold ProjectiveSetting.pointMeasExpOption
6627:+  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
6628:+  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
6629:+  intro a ha
6630:+  exact absurd (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2 (by simp)

6689:+theorem regroup_line_answer_sum_at {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ}
6690:+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
6691:+    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)

6709:+        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
6710:+        Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))

6776:+`Z`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products

6783:+    (F : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
6784:+      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → ℝ) :
6785:+    ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P), components.IsProbability ∧

6787:+          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
6788:+            (fun t => F (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
6789:+              (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
6790:+        avgOver components (fun c =>
6791:+          avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)

6793:+            (fun w => F ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2))) := by
6794:+  obtain ⟨components, hcomp, -, hZ⟩ := sublines.source_mixture

6798:+        (fun t => F (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
6799:+          (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) =
6800:+      avgOver ((subLinePointDist P sublines.D).map subLineZProjection) F := by
6801:+    rw [Distribution.avgOver_map, subLinePointDist, Distribution.avgOver_map,
6802:+      avgOver_prod]

6816:+/-- The overlap of the paired-line measurement at two source lines with the
6817:+expanded `Z`-point effect at a point, summed over the line answers.  This is
6818:+the integrand of the left-hand side of `lem:claim-17-3`, as a function of the
6819:+two source lines and the `Z`-point alone. -/
6820:+def zPointOverlapAt (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6821:+    (first second : Placement)
6822:+    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
6823:+      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) : ℝ :=
6824:+  ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
6825:+    (S.place first ((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.1.2).effect (fX, fZ)) *
6826:+      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2).effect (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))
6827:+
6828:+/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed overlap. -/
6829:+def zPointOverlap (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6830:+    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
6831:+      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) : ℝ :=
6832:+  ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
6833:+    (S.place .AA' ((lines.T .alice w.1.1 w.1.2).effect (fX, fZ)) *
6834:+      S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z w.2).effect (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))
6835:+
6836:+/-- At a pair of line-point pairs, the `Z`-point overlap is the overlap of the
6837:+evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed `Z`-point measurement; the
6838:+`X`-point of the first pair only labels the evaluation classes. -/
6839:+theorem zPointOverlap_eq_at (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6840:+    (first second : Placement)
6841:+    (w : LinePointPairSample P) :
6842:+    zPointOverlapAt lines first second ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2) =
6843:+      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
6844:+        stateQForm S.psiHat
6845:+          (S.place first
6846:+            (((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
6847:+              (evalOpt w.1.1 w.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt w.2.1 w.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
6848:+            S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2.2).effect o.2)) :=
6849:+  (regroup_line_answer_sum_at lines first second w.1.1 w.2.1 w.1.2 w.2.2
6850:+    (fun _ o2 => (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2.2).effect o2)).symm

6852:+/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
6853:+theorem zPointOverlap_eq (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6854:+    (w : LinePointPairSample P) :
6855:+    zPointOverlap lines ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2) =
6856:+      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
6857:+        stateQForm S.psiHat
6858:+          (S.place .AA'
6859:+            (((lines.T .alice w.1.1 w.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
6860:+              (evalOpt w.1.1 w.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt w.2.1 w.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
6861:+            S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z w.2.2).effect o.2)) := by
6862:+  exact zPointOverlap_eq_at lines .AA' .BA'' w

6864:+/-- The `Z`-point overlap is nonnegative. -/
6865:+theorem zPointOverlap_nonneg_at (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6866:+    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second)
6867:+    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
6868:+      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) :
6869:+    0 ≤ zPointOverlapAt lines first second w :=
6870:+  Finset.sum_nonneg fun fX _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun fZ _ =>
6871:+    stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg first second hopposite
6872:+      ((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.1.2).pos (fX, fZ))
6873:+      ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2).pos (evalOpt w.1.2 w.2 fZ)))
6874:+
6875:+/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
6876:+theorem zPointOverlap_nonneg (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6877:+    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
6878:+      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) :
6879:+    0 ≤ zPointOverlap lines w := by
6880:+  exact zPointOverlap_nonneg_at lines .AA' .BA'' trivial w

6882:+/-- The sub-line average of the `Z`-point overlap is at most one. -/
6883:+theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_zPointOverlap_le_one_at (sublines : SubLineWitness P)
6884:+    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
6885:+    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second) :
6886:+    avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
6887:+      avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
6888:+        (fun t => zPointOverlapAt lines first second (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
6889:+          (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) ≤ 1 := by
6890:+  obtain ⟨components, hcomp, hmix⟩ :=
6891:+    SubLineWitness.exists_avgOver_Z_eq_mixture P sublines (zPointOverlapAt lines first second)
6892:+  rw [hmix]
6893:+  have hc : ∀ c : SubLineComponent P,
6894:+      avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)
6895:+          (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
6896:+        (fun w => zPointOverlapAt lines first second ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.2.2)) ≤ 1 := by
6897:+    intro c
6898:+    have h := avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one
6899:+      (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)
6900:+        (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
6901:+      (fun w : LinePointPairSample P => S.placedMeasurement first
6902:+        ((lines.T first.side w.1.1 w.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
6903:+          (evalOpt w.1.1 w.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt w.2.1 w.2.2 fs.2)))
6904:+      (fun (w : LinePointPairSample P)
6905:+          (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)) =>
6906:+        S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z w.2.2).effect o.2))
6907:+      S.psiHat
6908:+      (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _
6909:+        (restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability P c.1 c.2.1)
6910:+        (restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability P c.1 c.2.2))
6911:+      S.psiHat_norm
6912:+      (fun w o => S.place_isProj _ (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj _ _ _ _))
6913:+      (fun w o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
6914:+    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect] at h
6915:+    rw [avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun w => zPointOverlap_eq_at lines first second w]
6916:+    exact h
6917:+  calc
6918:+    _ ≤ avgOver components (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := avgOver_mono _ _ _ hc
6919:+    _ = 1 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability components hcomp 1

6922:+theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_zPointOverlap_le_one (sublines : SubLineWitness P)

6924:+    avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
6925:+      avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
6926:+        (fun t => zPointOverlap lines (sample.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P
6927:+          (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) ≤ 1 := by

6994:+# A uniform point of the extended space from the directly indexed sub-line law
6995:+
6996:+The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
6997:+from the auxiliary `SubLineWitness` and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
6998:+This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
6999:+that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points. These
7000:+identities concern `directLinePointDist`. Transport to the source's seed-indexed
7001:+carrier remains open, as recorded in
7002:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, section
7003:+"Scalar estimates on the auxiliary subline law".
7004:+
7005:+## References
7006:+
7007:+These statements support `lem:claim-17-1` in
7008:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  The paper uses this sampling
7009:+fact at
7010:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1159-1166`.
7011:+-/

7021:+/-- A dependent mixture of a constant family is the constant law. -/
7022:+private theorem Distribution.bind_const_current {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
7023:+    (μ : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (ν : Distribution β) :
7024:+    Distribution.bind μ (fun _ => ν) = ν := by
7025:+  have hne : μ.support.Nonempty := by
7026:+    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
7027:+    by_contra hcard
7028:+    have hempty : μ.support = ∅ := by
7029:+      rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero]
7030:+      omega
7031:+    have htotal := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
7032:+    rw [hempty] at htotal
7033:+    simp at htotal
7034:+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
7035:+  · change μ.support.biUnion (fun _ => ν.support) = ν.support
7036:+    ext b
7037:+    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion]
7038:+    constructor
7039:+    · rintro ⟨a, -, hb⟩
7040:+      exact hb
7041:+    · intro hb
7042:+      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
7043:+      exact ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
7044:+  · funext b
7045:+    change (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b) = ν.weight b
7046:+    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hμ.weight_sum_eq_one, one_mul]
7047:+
7048:+/-- If every slice of a map of a pair carries the second uniform law to one
7049:+fixed law, then the map carries the uniform law of the pair to that law. -/
7050:+theorem uniformDistribution_map_uncurry {α β γ : Type*}
7051:+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
7052:+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
7053:+    (g : α × β → γ) (ν : Distribution γ)

7075:+    (V : Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) → (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :

7077:+        (fun p => lineRepMap (V (p.1.index, p.1.direction)) p.1.point +

7091:+          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × DirectScalarQ D)) :=

7097:+        ((uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map e).map

7100:+    rfl

7112:+          g (lineRepMap (V (s.index, s.direction)) s.point +
7113:+            t • V (s.index, s.direction)))) =

7120:+            p.2 • V (p.1.index, p.1.direction))) =

7122:+            (DirectLdSpace D × DirectScalarQ D)).map

7244:+/-!
7245:+# Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement
7246:+
7247:+The proof of `lem:claim-17-3` bounds, after its Cauchy--Schwarz step, the
7248:+deficit of the overlap between the evaluated pair-line measurement and the
7249:+expanded `Z`-point measurement at the `Z`-point of the sample.
7250:+This module derives that deficit from the
7251:+consistency of the evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint
7252:+point measurement and from the closeness of the joint point measurement to the
7253:+ordered point products. The derivation inserts the joint point measurement
7254:+on the point side, replaces it by the ordered product whose trailing factor is
7255:+the retained point effect, and sums the other factor, at the cost of three
7256:+square roots. The deficit is first bounded over an arbitrary probability
7257:+law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of two restricted
7258:+line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
7259:+The `_at` variants retain arbitrary opposite placements, including Bob at
7260:+`BBprime` and Alice at `ABdoubleprime`. The original statements are unchanged
7261:+specializations; register commutation does not assume symmetry of the state.
7262:+
7263:+## References
7264:+
7265:+The Z deficit is the quantity bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`
7266:+in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
7267:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
7268:+consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of
7269:+`lem:qld-4-10`.
7270:+-/
7271:+

7281:+/-! ## Completed point pairs -/
7282:+
7283:+/-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
7284:+classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
7285:+theorem sum_option_prod_eq_of_none {β γ : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
7286:+    (F : Option β × Option γ → ℝ) (h1 : ∀ o2, F (none, o2) = 0)
7287:+    (h2 : ∀ o1, F (o1, none) = 0) :
7288:+    (∑ o, F o) = ∑ bc : β × γ, F (some bc.1, some bc.2) := by
7289:+  calc (∑ o : Option β × Option γ, F o)
7290:+      = ∑ o1 : Option β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (o1, o2) := Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := F)
7291:+    _ = (∑ o2 : Option γ, F (none, o2)) +
7292:+          ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := Fintype.sum_option _
7293:+    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := by
7294:+        rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero fun o2 _ => h1 o2, zero_add]
7295:+    _ = ∑ b : β, (F (some b, none) + ∑ c : γ, F (some b, some c)) :=
7296:+        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => Fintype.sum_option _
7297:+    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ c : γ, F (some b, some c) := by
7298:+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
7299:+        rw [h2 (some b), zero_add]
7300:+    _ = ∑ bc : β × γ, F (some bc.1, some bc.2) :=
7301:+        (Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := fun bc : β × γ => F (some bc.1, some bc.2))).symm
7302:+
7303:+/-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
7304:+evaluations. -/
7305:+theorem completedPair_effect_some {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
7306:+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
7307:+    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (bc : β × γ) :
7308:+    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect (some bc.1, some bc.2) =
7309:+      Q.effect bc := by
7310:+  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
7311:+    show (Finset.univ.filter fun cd : β × γ =>
7312:+        (some cd.1, some cd.2) = (some bc.1, some bc.2)) = {bc} by
7313:+      ext cd; simp [Prod.ext_iff, eq_comm]]
7314:+  simp
7315:+
7316:+/-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
7317:+the completion. -/
7318:+theorem completedPair_effect_eq_zero {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
7319:+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
7320:+    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (o : Option β × Option γ)
7321:+    (ho : ∀ bc : β × γ, (some bc.1, some bc.2) ≠ o) :
7322:+    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o = 0 := by
7323:+  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
7324:+  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun bc hbc =>
7325:+    absurd (Finset.mem_filter.mp hbc).2 (ho bc)

7327:+/-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
7328:+theorem completedPair_isProjective {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
7329:+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
7330:+    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (hQ : Measurement.IsProjective Q) :
7331:+    Measurement.IsProjective (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)) := by
7332:+  intro o
7333:+  by_cases h : ∃ bc : β × γ, (some bc.1, some bc.2) = o
7334:+  · obtain ⟨bc, rfl⟩ := h
7335:+    rw [completedPair_effect_some]
7336:+    exact hQ bc
7337:+  · push Not at h
7338:+    rw [completedPair_effect_eq_zero Q o h]
7339:+    exact IsStarProjection.zero _

7345:+/-- A placed projection is a projection. -/
7346:+theorem place_isProj (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
7347:+    {E : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hE : IsProj E) :
7348:+    IsProj (S.place p E) := by
7349:+  refine isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩
7350:+  · change S.place p E * S.place p E = S.place p E
7351:+    rw [← place_mul, hE.isIdempotentElem.eq]
7352:+  · rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, ← place_conjTranspose,
7353:+      hE.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]

7355:+/-- Every effect of the completed expanded point measurement is a projection,
7356:+the `none` effect being zero. -/
7357:+theorem pointMeasExpOption_isProj (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
7358:+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
7359:+    (o : Option (PauliScalar P)) :
7360:+    IsProj ((S.pointMeasExpOption side W u).effect o) := by
7361:+  cases o with
7362:+  | none =>
7363:+    rw [S.pointMeasExpOption_effect_none]
7364:+    exact IsStarProjection.zero _
7365:+  | some a =>
7366:+    rw [S.pointMeasExpOption_effect_some]
7367:+    exact S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a

7369:+/-- The completed joint point measurement and a completed point product differ
7370:+only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
7371:+squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
7372:+product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
7373:+theorem sum_norm_place_completedPair_sub_sq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
7374:+    (p : Placement)
7375:+    (Q : Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
7376:+    (Gc : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P) →
7377:+      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
7378:+    (G : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
7379:+    (hsome : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P, Gc (some ab.1, some ab.2) = G ab)
7380:+    (hnone1 : ∀ o2, Gc (none, o2) = 0) (hnone2 : ∀ o1, Gc (o1, none) = 0) :
7381:+    (∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
7382:+        ‖applyOperatorToState
7383:+          (S.place p ((Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o) -
7384:+            S.place p (Gc o)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) =
7385:+      ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
7386:+        ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p (Q.effect ab) - S.place p (G ab))
7387:+          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 := by
7388:+  refine Eq.trans (sum_option_prod_eq_of_none _ ?_ ?_) ?_
7389:+  · intro o2
7390:+    rw [completedPair_effect_eq_zero Q (none, o2) (fun ab => by simp), hnone1,
7391:+      place_zero, sub_self]
7392:+    simp [applyOperatorToState]
7393:+  · intro o1
7394:+    rw [completedPair_effect_eq_zero Q (o1, none) (fun ab => by simp), hnone2,
7395:+      place_zero, sub_self]
7396:+    simp [applyOperatorToState]
7397:+  · refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ab _ => ?_
7398:+    rw [completedPair_effect_some, hsome]

7401:+and restricts to the ordered product on evaluated pairs. -/
7402:+theorem completedPair_norm_sq_sum_ZX (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) {δ : ℝ}

7408:+              (some ab.1, some ab.2))).effect o) -
7409:+            S.place p
7410:+              ((S.pointMeasExpOption p.side .Z z).effect o.2 *
7411:+                (S.pointMeasExpOption p.side .X x).effect o.1))
7412:+          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) =

7423:+  · intro o2
7424:+    rw [S.pointMeasExpOption_effect_none, mul_zero]

7431:+/-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
7432:+
7433:+/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
7434:+family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
7435:+outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
7436:+`W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
7437:+within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
7438:+with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
7439:+`Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
7440:+Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
7441:+the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
7442:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
7443:+theorem one_sub_overlap_le_of_consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
7444:+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
7445:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
7446:+    (μ : Distribution X) (A Q : X → Measurement α ι) (R W : X → α → Op ι)
7447:+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
7448:+    (hQ : ∀ x, Measurement.IsProjective (Q x)) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
7449:+    (hAQ : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((Q x).effect a))
7450:+    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a))
7451:+    (hAW : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a))
7452:+    (hWR : ∀ x a, W x a * R x a = W x a)
7453:+    (hnonneg : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a))
7454:+    (η ζ : ℝ)
7455:+    (hcons : consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
7456:+      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ ≤ η)
7457:+    (hdist : opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (Q x).effect a)
7458:+      (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ ≤ ζ) :
7459:+    1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) ≤
7460:+      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
7461:+  set ovQ := avgOver μ (fun x =>
7462:+    ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a)) with hovQ
7463:+  have h1 : 1 - ovQ ≤ η := by
7464:+    rw [← consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ A Q ψ hμ hψ]
7465:+    exact hcons
7466:+  have hovQ_nonneg : 0 ≤ ovQ :=
7467:+    avgOver_nonneg μ _ fun x => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => hnonneg x a
7468:+  have hovQ_le : ovQ ≤ 1 :=
7469:+    avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ hμ hψ
7470:+      (fun x a => hQ x a) hAQ
7471:+  have h1' : 1 - ovQ ≤ Real.sqrt η := by
7472:+    have h0 : 0 ≤ 1 - ovQ := by linarith
7473:+    calc 1 - ovQ = Real.sqrt ((1 - ovQ) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq h0).symm
7474:+      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (by nlinarith)
7475:+  -- comparing `Q` with `W` under the weight `A`
7476:+  have hWconj : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a) =
7477:+      stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a)ᴴ) := by
7478:+    intro x a
7479:+    rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a),
7480:+      Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, measurement_effect_hermitian]
7481:+    congr 1
7482:+    have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (hAW x a).eq
7483:+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
7484:+      measurement_effect_hermitian] at h
7485:+    exact h
7486:+  have h2 : |ovQ - avgOver μ (fun x =>
7487:+      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤ Real.sqrt ζ := by
7488:+    rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hWconj x a]
7489:+    exact abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq μ A
7490:+      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ hμ hψ ζ hdist
7491:+  -- replacing `Q R` by `W R = W`
7492:+  have h4 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
7493:+      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
7494:+        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a))| ≤
7495:+      Real.sqrt ζ := by
7496:+    have hpt : ∀ x,
7497:+        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
7498:+          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a)) =
7499:+        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (((Q x).effect a - W x a) * R x a)) := by
7500:+      intro x
7501:+      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
7502:+      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
7503:+      rw [sub_mul, hWR]
7504:+      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
7505:+    rw [← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
7506:+    have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_sqrt_of_isProj' μ A
7507:+      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a - W x a) R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
7508:+      (fun x a => (hAQ x a).sub_right (hAW x a))
7509:+    refine hcs.trans (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ?_)
7510:+    have hdist' : avgOver μ (fun x =>
7511:+        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState ((Q x).effect a - (W x a)ᴴ) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤ ζ :=
7512:+      hdist
7513:+    refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ hdist'
7514:+    refine avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
7515:+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, measurement_effect_hermitian]
7516:+  -- inserting `Q` before `R`
7517:+  have h5 : |avgOver μ (fun x =>
7518:+      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) -
7519:+        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a))| ≤
7520:+      Real.sqrt η := by
7521:+    have hpt : ∀ x,
7522:+        (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) -
7523:+          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((Q x).effect a * R x a))) =
7524:+        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * ((1 - (Q x).effect a) * R x a)) := by
7525:+      intro x
7526:+      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
7527:+      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
7528:+      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, sub_mul, mul_sub]
7529:+    rw [abs_sub_comm, ← avgOver_sub, avgOver_congr μ _ _ hpt]
7530:+    have hcs := abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt μ A
7531:+      (fun x a => 1 - (Q x).effect a) R ψ (fun x a => (hQ x a).one_sub)
7532:+      (fun x a => (Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAQ x a))
7533:+    have hfirst : avgOver μ (fun x =>
7534:+        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - (Q x).effect a))) = 1 - ovQ := by
7535:+      have hx : ∀ x,
7536:+          (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - (Q x).effect a))) =
7537:+            1 - ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a) := by
7538:+        intro x
7539:+        rw [← sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
7540:+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
7541:+        simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
7542:+      rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ hx, avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ]
7543:+    have hsecond : avgOver μ (fun x =>
7544:+        ∑ a, stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (R x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a)) ≤ 1 := by
7545:+      rw [avgOver_congr μ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
7546:+        stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (hR x a) (hAR x a)]
7547:+      exact avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A R ψ hμ hψ hR hAR
7548:+    rw [hfirst] at hcs
7549:+    calc
7550:+      _ ≤ _ := hcs
7551:+      _ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - ovQ) * 1 := by
7552:+        refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
7553:+        rw [← Real.sqrt_one]
7554:+        exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hsecond
7555:+      _ = Real.sqrt (1 - ovQ) := mul_one _
7556:+      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h1
7557:+  have h2' := abs_le.mp h2
7558:+  have h4' := abs_le.mp h4
7559:+  have h5' := abs_le.mp h5
7560:+  linarith [h2'.1, h4'.1, h5'.1, h2'.2, h4'.2, h5'.2]

7562:+/-! ## The two placed deficits -/
7563:+
7564:+/-- A pair of line-point pairs of the source space: the sample type of the
7565:+consistency display of `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
7566:+abbrev LinePointPairSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
7567:+  (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) ×
7568:+    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
7569:+
7570:+section Placed
7571:+
7572:+variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ δP : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
7573:+  {points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ}
7574:+
7575:+/-- The `Z`-point deficit of the evaluated pair-line measurement over a
7576:+probability law on pairs of line-point pairs, from the consistency of the
7577:+evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint point measurement
7578:+and the closeness of the latter to the `Z`-then-`X` product.  This is the
7579:+deficit bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
7580:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
7581:+theorem CombinedLinesWitness.one_sub_Z_overlap_le_at
7582:+    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
7583:+    (first second : Placement) (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second)
7584:+    (ν : Distribution (LinePointPairSample P)) (hν : ν.IsProbability) (η ζ : ℝ)
7585:+    (hcons : consistencyDefect ν
7586:+      (fun s o => S.place first
7587:+        (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7588:+          (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o))
7589:+      (fun s o => S.place second
7590:+        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7591:+          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
7592:+      S.psiHat ≤ η)
7593:+    (hZX : opFamilyDistSq ν
7594:+      (fun s o => S.place second
7595:+        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7596:+          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
7597:+      (fun s o => S.place second
7598:+        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
7599:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1))
7600:+      S.psiHat ≤ ζ) :
7601:+    1 - avgOver ν (fun s =>
7602:+      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
7603:+        stateQForm S.psiHat
7604:+          (S.place first
7605:+            (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7606:+              (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
7607:+            S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))) ≤
7608:+      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
7609:+  have hQproj : ∀ s : LinePointPairSample P,
7610:+      Measurement.IsProjective (S.placedMeasurement second
7611:+        ((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2))) :=
7612:+    fun s => S.placedMeasurement_isProjective _ _
7613:+      (completedPair_isProjective _ (points.projective _ _ _))
7614:+  have hRproj : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
7615:+      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
7616:+      IsProj (S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2)) :=
7617:+    fun s o => S.place_isProj _ (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj _ _ _ _)
7618:+  have hWR : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
7619:+      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
7620:+      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7621:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) *
7622:+        S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) =
7623:+      S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7624:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2) := by
7625:+    intro s o
7626:+    have hlocal : (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7627:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
7628:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 =
7629:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7630:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 := by
7631:+      rw [mul_assoc, (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .Z s.2.2 o.2).isIdempotentElem.eq]
7632:+    exact (ProjectiveSetting.place_mul S second _ _).symm.trans
7633:+      (congrArg (S.place second) hlocal)
7634:+  have hnonneg : ∀ (s : LinePointPairSample P)
7635:+      (o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P)),
7636:+      0 ≤ stateQForm S.psiHat
7637:+        (S.place first
7638:+          (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7639:+            (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
7640:+          S.place second
7641:+            (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7642:+              (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o)) :=
7643:+    fun s o => stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg first second hopposite
7644:+      (((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7645:+        (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).pos o)
7646:+      (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7647:+        (some ab.1, some ab.2)).pos o))
7648:+  have hdist : opFamilyDistSq ν
7649:+      (fun s o => S.place second
7650:+        (((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7651:+          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
7652:+      (fun s o => (S.place second
7653:+        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7654:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))ᴴ)
7655:+      S.psiHat ≤ ζ := by
7656:+    refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ hZX
7657:+    unfold opFamilyDistSq
7658:+    refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun s => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun o _ => ?_
7659:+    have hlocal : ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7660:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2)ᴴ =
7661:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
7662:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 := by
7663:+      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
7664:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .Z s.2.2 o.2).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
7665:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj second.side .X s.1.2 o.1).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
7666:+    have hplace : (S.place second
7667:+        ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7668:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))ᴴ =
7669:+        S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
7670:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1) :=
7671:+      (ProjectiveSetting.place_conjTranspose S second _).symm.trans
7672:+        (congrArg (S.place second) hlocal)
7673:+    dsimp only
7674:+    rw [hplace]
7675:+  exact one_sub_overlap_le_of_consistencyDefect ν
7676:+    (fun s => S.placedMeasurement first
7677:+      ((lines.T first.side s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7678:+        (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)))
7679:+    (fun s => S.placedMeasurement second
7680:+      ((points.Q second.side s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)))
7681:+    (fun s o => S.place second ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))
7682:+    (fun s o => S.place second
7683:+      ((S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .X s.1.2).effect o.1 *
7684:+        (S.pointMeasExpOption second.side .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))
7685:+    S.psiHat hν S.psiHat_norm hQproj hRproj
7686:+    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
7687:+    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
7688:+    (fun s o => S.place_comm first second hopposite _ _)
7689:+    hWR hnonneg η ζ hcons hdist
7690:+
7691:+/-- The original first-player specialization of the opposite-placement estimate. -/
7692:+theorem CombinedLinesWitness.one_sub_Z_overlap_le
7693:+    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness S points δP)
7694:+    (ν : Distribution (LinePointPairSample P)) (hν : ν.IsProbability) (η ζ : ℝ)
7695:+    (hcons : consistencyDefect ν
7696:+      (fun s o => S.place .AA'
7697:+        (((lines.T .alice s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7698:+          (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o))
7699:+      (fun s o => S.place .BA''
7700:+        (((points.Q .bob s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7701:+          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
7702:+      S.psiHat ≤ η)
7703:+    (hZX : opFamilyDistSq ν
7704:+      (fun s o => S.place .BA''
7705:+        (((points.Q .bob s.1.2 s.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
7706:+          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o))
7707:+      (fun s o => S.place .BA''
7708:+        ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z s.2.2).effect o.2 *
7709:+          (S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .X s.1.2).effect o.1))
7710:+      S.psiHat ≤ ζ) :
7711:+    1 - avgOver ν (fun s =>
7712:+      ∑ o : Option (PauliScalar P) × Option (PauliScalar P),
7713:+        stateQForm S.psiHat
7714:+          (S.place .AA'
7715:+            (((lines.T .alice s.1.1 s.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
7716:+              (evalOpt s.1.1 s.1.2 fs.1, evalOpt s.2.1 s.2.2 fs.2)).effect o) *
7717:+            S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExpOption .bob .Z s.2.2).effect o.2))) ≤
7718:+      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
7719:+  exact lines.one_sub_Z_overlap_le_at .AA' .BA'' trivial ν hν η ζ hcons hZX
7720:+

7722:+end Placed

7724:+/-! ## The two deficits over a product of restricted line-point laws -/
7725:+
7726:+/-- Every restricted line-point law has total mass one. -/
7727:+theorem restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams)
7728:+    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
7729:+    (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i).IsProbability := by
7730:+  cases kind
7731:+  · change (restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i).IsProbability
7732:+    exact restrictedALineDist_isProbability P.toLdParams i
7733:+  · change (restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i).IsProbability
7734:+    exact restrictedDLineDist_isProbability P.toLdParams i
7735:+
7736:+/-- The point marginal of a restricted line-point law is uniform. -/
7737:+theorem restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
7738:+    (i : Fin P.m) :
7739:+    (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i).map Prod.snd =
7740:+      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) := by
7741:+  rw [restrictedLinePointDist_eq_map_prod, Distribution.map_map]
7742:+  exact Distribution.prod_map_fst _ _ (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _
7743:+    (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P i) (uniformDistribution_isProbability _))
7744:+
7745:+/-- The pair of points of a product of two restricted line-point laws is a
7746:+uniform pair. -/
7747:+theorem prod_restrictedLinePointDist_map_points (P : AdmissibleParams)
7748:+    (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
7749:+    (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i)
7750:+        (restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j)).map (fun s => (s.1.2, s.2.2)) =
7751:+      uniformDistribution
7752:+        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
7753:+  have h : Distribution.prod ((restrictedLinePointDist P kindX i).map Prod.snd)
7754:+      ((restrictedLinePointDist P kindZ j).map Prod.snd) =
7755:+      uniformDistribution
7756:+        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
7757:+    rw [restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd, restrictedLinePointDist_map_snd,
7758:+      uniformDistribution_prod]
7759:+  rw [← h, Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.prod_map_right,
7760:+    Distribution.map_map]
7761:+
7762:+/-- A state-dependent distance between two families depending on the pair of
7763:+points only, averaged over a product of two restricted line-point laws, is the

## 9. The findings ledger

`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
status signal; the REST `line` field lied.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]

/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
inductive LineKind where
  | axis
  | diagonal
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A seed-bearing line description for blueprint
`def:line-point-dist`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.

An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal

/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed

/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
  | .axis base _ _ => base
  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base

/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
not apply a second projection. -/
def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
  match line with
  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction

/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
geometric direction. -/
theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
  cases line with
  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed

/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
  cases line with

(u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)

/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
      intro j hj
      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])

/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)

/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper

## Notation Consistency
Notation must be **internally consistent** across the entire blueprint and **close to what the Lean code expresses**:

- **Indices**: 0-indexed where matching `Fin n` in Lean
- **Finite fields / alphabets**: use standard notation for the alphabet $\Sigma$ and finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$
- **Measurements**: use standard quantum measurement notation (projective measurements, POVMs)
- **Strategies**: quantum strategies for nonlocal games should use standard notation from the literature
- **Expansion**: use standard notation for graph expansion parameters
- **Macros** (in `macros/common.tex`): define project-specific macros and use them consistently

The original reference controls notation whenever it gives a usable convention.
If the blueprint needs a different symbol, index convention, or name in order to
match Lean, introduce it explicitly and relate it to the paper notation in the
same paragraph.  Do not let a `\lean{...}` tag, a Lean namespace, or a file name
be the only explanation of a changed term.

When a public Lean declaration is a formalization-only auxiliary lemma, the
blueprint should say so before listing the declaration.  The surrounding prose
should identify the paper theorem, equation, or construction that the auxiliary
lemma supports, and should avoid making the auxiliary name look like a named
result from the source article.

## What NOT to Put in the Blueprint
- **Lean identifier names in math text.** Write "the self-improvement lemma", never "the `selfImprovement` step". The `\lean{LDT.selfImprovement}` tag handles the linking.
- **Implementation details.** Don't say "bundled as an element of the Euclidean space" or "using `EuclideanSpace.equiv`". Describe the mathematical object.
- **Ad-hoc notation.** Don't invent superscripts or subscripts to distinguish from existing notation. Use standard conventions.
- **Function-call syntax.** Use mathematical notation, not programming notation.
- **Redundant definitions.** If two blueprint definitions describe the same mathematical object, consolidate them. Each definition should introduce genuinely new mathematical content.
- **Lean namespace prefixes in prose.** Don't write "the `LDT.PastingLemma`" — write "the pasting lemma".

## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
look as if the paper stated them.

- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
  anchored paper passage, or blueprint label it supports. Blueprint line
  ranges are derived review context, not stored docstring citations; resolve a
  label with `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve <label>`.
- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
  Lean proof.
- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
  used.
- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
  proof remains tracked as incomplete.

- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.

4:# The branch data of the sub-line sampling procedure
5:
6:The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma draws a line kind, a stored
7:extended coordinate, and an unrestricted extended direction, and forms from

9:stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with the

10:and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn

12:two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
13:diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
14:decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
15:from the two seeds.

18:of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
19:sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
20:affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
21:extended-line marginal.

4:/-!
5:# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
6:
7:This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
8:the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
9:is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
10:coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
11:the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
12:point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
13:commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
14:canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
15:field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
16:the same three coordinate ranges.

21:blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
22:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
23:The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
24:445--480, paper lines 970--989.
25:-/
35:/-! ## Linearity of the coordinate blocks -/
37:/-- The `X` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
38:Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
39:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
44:/-- The `Z` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.

53:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
58:/-- The `Z` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar

60:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

\chapter{Combining the bases and applying the classical test}
\label{chap:qpbt-combining}
% Paper subsection label sec:combining kept for cross-reference fidelity; the
% companion label sec:apply-ldt is attached to the corresponding section below.
% Source: references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex,
% lines 680-1414 (subsections "Combining the X and Z measurements" and
% "Applying the classical low-degree test").
\label{sec:combining}

Throughout this chapter we work in the setting of
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}: a projective strategy for the Pauli basis
test game succeeds with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all operators act
relative to the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ on registers
$\mathsf{A}\,\mathsf{A}'\,\mathsf{A}''\,\mathsf{B}\,\mathsf{B}'\,\mathsf{B}''$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}), where each of the four ancilla
registers $\mathsf{A}'$, $\mathsf{A}''$, $\mathsf{B}'$, and $\mathsf{B}''$
--- two appended per player, the pair $\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''$
(respectively $\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$) holding $M$ EPR pairs of local
dimension $q$ --- is a register of $M = 2^m$ qudits with Hilbert space
isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$.
We write $q = 2^t$ (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and
$\tr:\F_q\to\F_2$ for the subfield trace. The points measurements
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}), their binary refinements
\[
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b
	= \sum_{a \,:\, \tr(ar) = b} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\,,
	\qquad r \in \F_q,\ b \in \F_2
\]
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}), and the lines
measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{f}$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-line-measurement}) are those constructed in
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}, and $\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}(\eps)$ and
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)$ denote the error functions of
Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} and Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons},
respectively.

A subscript such as $(\,\cdot\,)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ indicates the pair of
registers on which an operator acts; the two bipartitions in use are
$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ versus $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ and
$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ versus $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$. The state-dependent
distances $\approx_\delta$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) and
$\simeq_\delta$ (Definition~\ref{def:consistency}) are taken with respect to
$\ket{\hat\psi}$ and averaged over the stated question distribution, and
``all symmetric equivalents'' of an approximation is meant in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}. Between scalars, $\alpha
\approx_\delta \beta$ means $|\alpha - \beta| \le O(\delta)$. For sums of
measurement operators over outcomes satisfying a predicate we use the bracket
notation of Definition~\ref{def:bracket}; for instance
$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
= \sum_{f_X,f_Z \,:\, f_X(x)=a,\ f_Z(z)=b} T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}$.
For a line $\ell$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) and $k \in \N$ we write
$\deg_k(\ell)$ for the set of polynomial functions on $\ell$ of degree at most
$k$ in the line parameter, and
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q) = \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$
(Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}) for the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$. Elements of
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ enter the statements and proofs of this chapter
only through the representatives themselves and their evaluations; evaluation
identifies the representatives with the induced polynomial functions
(Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}), bijectively precisely when
$d \le q-1$, a bound that admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ does not imply and that
is not assumed here. The restriction of an element of
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ to a line has total degree at most $md$.

\section{Combined point measurements}

The measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}$ and
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}$ commute only approximately. The first goal of
this chapter is to construct a single projective measurement that
simultaneously measures both, first at points and then along lines. The
construction of the combined point measurement proceeds in three steps: the
binary refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}$ and
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index
pair $(r,s)$, and the following result of Natarajan and
Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
assembled by Fourier averaging.

/-!
# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma

This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
from the two seeds.

The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
extended-line marginal.

## References

The construction is the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
-/

/-!
# Placement calculus on the expanded state

This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
`def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.

## References

The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1003-1030`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.  The
EPR-exchange invariance is the element `U_σ U_θ` of
`lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1032-1130`, which needs no
symmetry of the strategy; its use for `lem:qld-4-10` is analyzed in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
-/

/-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/

/-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AA'.side)) :
    S.place .AA' O =
      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron O
          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm

/-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
    S.place .BA'' O =
      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_right S O).symm

/-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
theorem place_AB''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AB''.side)) :
    S.place .AB'' O =
      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron O
          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm

/-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
theorem place_BB'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BB'.side)) :
    S.place .BB' O =
      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_right S O).symm

/-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
theorem reindexOp_conjTranspose {ι κ : Type*} (e : ι ≃ κ) (M : Op κ) :
    reindexOp e Mᴴ = (reindexOp e M)ᴴ := by
  ext i j
  rfl

/-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
theorem reindexOp_nonneg {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
    (e : ι ≃ κ) {M : Op κ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    0 ≤ reindexOp e M := by
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite κ
  rw [Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef] at hM ⊢
  exact hM.submatrix e.symm.symm

/-! ## The placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism -/

/-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
theorem place_mul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    ∀ (p : Placement) (A B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
      S.place p (A * B) = S.place p A * S.place p B
  | .AA', A, B => by
      classical
      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq,
        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .BA'', A, B => by
      classical
      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq,
        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
        mul_one, mul_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .BB', A, B => by
      classical
      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq,
        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
        mul_one, mul_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .AB'', A, B => by
      classical
      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq,
        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
      all_goals rfl

/-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
space. -/
theorem place_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :
    S.place p (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) = 1 := by
  ext i j
  cases p <;>
    · simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.one_apply, Prod.ext_iff]
      split_ifs <;> simp_all

/-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators. -/
theorem place_finsetSum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {γ : Type*}
    (s : Finset γ) (O : γ → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
    S.place p (∑ x ∈ s, O x) = ∑ x ∈ s, S.place p (O x) := by
  ext i j
  cases p <;>
    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul,
      Finset.mul_sum]

/-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
theorem place_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    ∀ (p : Placement) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
      S.place p Aᴴ = (S.place p A)ᴴ
  | .AA', A => by
      rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .BA'', A => by
      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .BB', A => by
      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
        Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
      all_goals rfl
  | .AB'', A => by
      rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
      all_goals rfl
